finding.claim: Webhook events are delivered to every active subscription regardless of owner, so any authenticated operator can receive other tenants' host names, host/network/CA IDs and cert fingerprints.
finding.source: POST /api/v1/webhook-subscriptions (internal/api/server.go:245, handler internal/api/webhooks.go:67-112). Any authenticated operator; events omitted so all event types match (internal/webhook/store_source.go:74-77).
finding.sink: StoreSource.TargetsFor (internal/webhook/store_source.go:43-62) -> ListActiveWebhookSubscriptions (internal/store/sqlite_webhooks.go:126-128, WHERE active = 1, no owner filter) -> Dispatcher.dispatch POST (internal/webhook/webhook.go:213-222).

trace.note: Create subscription; any operator may create; only allow_private is admin-gated (line 73).
Owner recorded but never consulted during delivery.
wantsEvent returns true for empty events list.
host.deleted emitted for any tenant's host.
hostEventData exposes host_id, host_name, network_id, ca_id.
host.enrolled emitted with fingerprint.
Emit attaches no tenant key to the event.
targets() appends all source targets.
Global active-subscription query.

finding.guards_checked: canAccessWebhookSub (internal/api/webhooks.go:30-35) scopes CRUD only, not delivery. ValidateWebhookURL (internal/config/server.go:188-203) is SSRF-only. wantsEvent filters by event type only. The SSE stream (internal/web/events.go:92-117) and API list endpoints do scope by owner, so this path is inconsistent. internal/simtest/tenant_isolation_test.go has no webhook coverage.

finding.claim: Disabling an operator does not revoke their enrolled hosts. Their agents keep passing poll authentication, receive re-rendered network config and the CA blocklist, and keep a valid mesh certificate for up to 30 days (renewal is refused but the existing cert is not blocklisted).
finding.source: Admin disables an operator via the API (internal/api/operators.go:93-105) or web UI (internal/web/operators.go:184).
finding.sink: Agent poll GET /api/v1/agent/updates (internal/api/updates.go:40-279) returns config and blocklist to the disabled owner's hosts.

trace.note: DisableOperator updates operator status, deletes sessions, revokes API keys only; no host blocking.
Poll verifies host signature and nonce; does not check owner status.
Revocation check only tests host.Status == blocked.
Global CA blocklist returned to host.
Config re-rendered for host when network version changes.
Renewal attempted; failure is logged and polling continues.
checkIssuanceAllowed refuses renewal for disabled owner.
Agent cert lifetime is 30 days.

finding.guards_checked: Enrollment blocked for disabled owners (internal/api/enroll.go:93-105). Renewal refused via checkIssuanceAllowed (updates.go:297-299). Sessions and API keys of the disabled operator are revoked (sqlite_operators.go:337-345). The code comment at updates.go:293-296 states dropping off at cert expiry is intended, so severity depends on the threat model.

finding.claim: The TOTP second factor has no per-session or per-account failure counter, so a password holder can make unlimited TOTP guesses within the 5-minute pending window, limited only by the per-IP auth rate limiter.
finding.source: POST /ui/login/totp by an attacker holding the operator's password (pending_totp session).

trace.note: Password login with TOTP enabled creates pending_totp session with 5-minute lifetime (pendingTOTPMaxLife, session.go:23-24).
verifyTOTPWithTimestep checks code; one-time consumption via ConsumeOperatorTOTPTimestep (line 135).
Failed code path only writes audit row and re-renders; no RecordFailedLoginAttempt or lockout.
Only throttle is rateLimitMiddleware(auth) on POST /ui/login/totp.

finding.guards_checked: Single-use TOTP timestep consumption (handlers.go:135). Per-IP auth rate limit (web.go:314). Password-path lockout (session.go:137) does not apply to TOTP failures.
